newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis bids mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis bids mostly unchanged.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were mostly unchanged Tuesday at interior and Gulf locations, and grain merchandisers said farmer selling was virtually nonexistent.
"We certainly didn't see a lot of offers yesterday. It was a very quiet day," one Oklahoma dealer said.

Meanwhile, most hard red winter wheat growing areas failed to get any precipitation Monday night as storms bypassed the region, dropping heavy rains only in eastern Kansas and Oklahoma. Merchandisers said they were beginning to hear concerns about low soil moisture levels.
"We got all the wind from the storm but none of the rain -- and we could use some moisture right now," a south central Kansas dealer said.
"We only got about four-tenths of an inch last night and we could have used more. There's no moisture in the forecast now for at least another five days," a northern Oklahoma dealer said.
The weekly state crop reports, released Monday, showed that HRW wheat condition declined slightly in Oklahoma and Texas during the week ended Sunday, but remained mostly unchanged in Kansas.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
